# Shortcut audit (generated by `scripts/run_audit.py`)

Each feature on its own is given to a depth-2 decision tree. The score is the mean AUROC over 5-fold stratified cross-validation. `overall` = Normal vs all attacks; each attack column = that attack vs Normal. A feature is **suspect** if its AUROC is >= 0.95 overall or for at least one attack type. Text features (proto, service, state) use all their one-hot columns together.

- Suspect overall: 0 features: 
- Suspect for at least one attack type: 5 features: `sttl`, `sbytes`, `smean`, `dloss`, `dbytes`

## Classification

- **Identity artifact**: reveals which machine or lab setup produced the flow. Candidate for removal.
- **Real behaviour**: describes what the flow or host did. Kept, even if its AUROC is high.
- Being computed from IP addresses does not by itself make a feature an identity artifact: a count does not reveal which IP it was.

| feature | type | overall AUROC | highest single-attack AUROC | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sttl` | identity artifact | 0.846 | 0.963 (Analysis) | Time-to-live set by the sender's operating system, minus one per router hop. It tells which machine sent the flow and how far away it is, not what the flow did. |
| `sbytes` | real behaviour | 0.706 | 0.962 (Analysis) | Bytes sent: what the flow carried. |
| `smean` | real behaviour | 0.694 | 0.956 (Analysis) | Mean packet size sent: what the flow carried. |
| `dloss` | real behaviour | 0.670 | 0.951 (Analysis) | Packets retransmitted or dropped by the destination: how the exchange went. |
| `dbytes` | real behaviour | 0.635 | 0.972 (Analysis) | Bytes received: what the flow carried. |
| `dttl` | identity artifact | 0.832 | 0.935 (Generic) | Same as sttl, for the reply direction (identifies the responding machine). |
| `ct_state_ttl` | identity artifact | 0.852 | 0.950 (Generic) | Computed directly from state together with ranges of sttl/dttl, so it carries the same TTL information. |
| `is_sm_ips_ports` | unclear (leans artifact) | 0.504 | 0.504 (Fuzzers) | Directly encodes whether source and destination IP and port are equal. Equal addresses can be real behaviour (for example a LAND attack), but in this data the value 1 occurs only in Normal rows, mostly ARP, so here it marks a property of the lab's normal traffic. Its AUROC is low only because it is rare. |
| `stcpb` | noise | 0.523 | 0.802 (Generic) | Random initial TCP sequence number chosen by the sender. Its only signal is whether it is zero (no TCP handshake), which swin already carries. |
| `dtcpb` | noise | 0.523 | 0.802 (Generic) | Same as stcpb for the reply direction. |

## TTL features: what the AUROC does not show

No TTL feature reaches the threshold overall, but they rank near the top. An unlimited-depth tree gives overall AUROC `sttl` 0.846 (depth 2: 0.846), `dttl` 0.832 (depth 2: 0.832), `ct_state_ttl` 0.853 (depth 2: 0.852), so the limit is in the values themselves, not the tree: some TTL values occur only in Normal traffic, while the values most attacks use are shared with part of Normal. `sttl`:

| 0 | 766 | 1.000 | 0.009 |
| 1 | 81 | 1.000 | 0.001 |

| 31 | 55,713 | 1.000 | 0.653 |
| 62 | 24,735 | 0.237 | 0.069 |

## Other reviewed features

- `is_sm_ips_ports` = 1 in 649 rows; classes: {'Normal': 649}; proto: {'arp': 643, 'tcp': 6}.
- `stcpb`: zero in 24.2% of rows. AUROC of the value: 0.523; of only "is zero": 0.523; of the value among non-zero rows: 0.500. "Non-zero" agrees with `swin` > 0 on 98.9% of rows.
- `dtcpb`: zero in 24.2% of rows. AUROC of the value: 0.523; of only "is zero": 0.523; of the value among non-zero rows: 0.500. "Non-zero" agrees with `swin` > 0 on 98.9% of rows.
